text:
Research supports testing diagnostic correctness before trusting quality claims. A [2024 recommender metamorphic-testing study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0950584924000156) evaluates reliability through expected relationships between executions. Applied here, useful proposed mutations include disabled branches, shuffled titles/descriptions, corrupted attention masks, and mismatched checkpoint exports. Each probe should detect its relevant fault while accepting valid transformations; unused text should have no effect. Positive score rescaling must preserve ranking metrics for fixed candidates and consistent tie handling, although losses and margins may change. These are proposed checks, not evidence that this toolkit already detects failures.

Sampled ranking requires particular caution. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show that sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation; small candidate sets also blur distinctions between metrics. [RecSys 2025 research](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) examines sampling reliability, while [RecSys 2026 work](https://mdw.ekstrandom.net/pubs/recsys26-eval) studies agreement between evaluation designs and dense relevance judgments. Consequently, HR@10 against 99 negatives and full-catalog recommendation measure different tasks; diagnostic sensitivity to candidate count, sampling distribution, and seed deserves explicit measurement.

For this benchmark, retain pinned host macro validation HR@10 as the selection criterion. Within the shared budget, compare diagnostic changes with host-exposed validation changes across all four datasets, reporting per-category results alongside the macro average. Use training-prefix audits only as auxiliary measurements because fitted histories can overstate generalization. Check exported-predictor score and ranking agreement directly. Mutation detection establishes fault sensitivity; improved training margins or embedding alignment alone does not establish recommendation quality.
